findings.reason: the section must be rewritten against the code (or marked historical), because as written it dispatches a node to build an export gate that exists.
findings.text: §2 opens "`export.py:1242` writes `\"status\": \"active\"` as a literal", but at HEAD line 1242 appends the `bound_adjacent` gate issue and the status assignment is `node[\"status\"] if \"status\" in node else \"active\"` at export.py:1575, behind the pre-existing gate registry `GATE_CATALOG_STATUS` (export.py:184) and the `null_catalog_status` refusal (export.py:2918) — so the section describes a defect that is already closed and proposes a gate the file already owns; a reader cannot tell which part of §2 is still to do

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is proposed; every mechanism is placed in an existing owner (`imas_codex/standard_names/export.py`, `imas_codex/graph/cypher_property_check.py`, `imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py`), and the one substantial new routine, the static touch-checker, hides a per-alias parse behind one function.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5's treatments are re-homed as `reconcile_*` maintenance steps in `run_sn_pools`, but the design sections never name the sequence owner or the reconcile functions that already implement three of the five footgun rows.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds a refusal (`null_catalog_status`, `export.py:2918`) and §5a adds a public definition (`audit_standard_name_touch`, `cypher_property_check.py:611`) without either section's text naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 states its defect at `export.py:1242`, and no such write exists at that line; the machinery §2, §4 and §5a propose is already present in modules the sections do not name, so the design reads as new work over an owned surface.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two candidate wrappers (`record_catalog_import_provenance` over `guard_catalog_write_payloads`, and the `reconcile_*` treatment functions over `_global_maintenance_call`) each carry the section's stated reason why the existing mechanism cannot be extended: the allow-list shape and the scope/bypass pairing.
